official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document H scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document H provides Building Regulations guidance for foul water drainage and disposal, including above- and below-ground drainage, pipe sizing and access provisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building-control sewer proximity information
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current building-control application guidance requires drainage precautions to be described where work is over or within 3 metres of a drain, public or private sewer or disposal main.

official_measurement_examples.name: New sewage treatment system approval
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance says a new sewage treatment system requires Building Regulations approval and may also require planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Existing discharge caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance says an existing septic or treatment-plant discharge that does not meet general binding rules must be corrected, connected to sewer where reasonable, or permitted where required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Unsatisfactory drainage power
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building Act 1984 section 59 gives local authorities powers to require satisfactory provision or remedial work for specified defective or prejudicial drainage.

official_measurement_examples.name: Drain repair notice period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building Act 1984 section 61 generally requires at least 24 hours notice to the local authority before repair, reconstruction or alteration of an underground drain communicating with a sewer or cesspool, except emergencies.

official_measurement_examples.name: Non-mains hierarchy
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official local building-control guidance applies a hierarchy favouring sewer connection where practicable before non-mains options such as septic tanks, treatment plants or cesspools.

official_measurement_examples.name: Drainage ownership crossing land
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official planning guidance notes that drainage crossing land not owned by an applicant can require separate landowner notices or rights; drainage design does not confer those rights.
